text_fidelity_a:
UVPaqlite Mini (6 x 4) I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased; this was the second brightest, and was the most useful size. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 45 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. By 60 and 90 minutes, the Paqlite Mini was still faintly visible, but only just barely.

It glowed brighter and longer than either the [[ASIN:B0068QL4E6 Tooblite]] and [[ASIN:B0068QN7VO Tooblite Mini]]. While the Tooblite designs are convenient for many tasks, the UVPaqlite Mini is the lightest of the bunch, and quite compact. While it doesn't seem quite as durable as the two Tooblites, the rugged vacuum-sealed packet still feels like it would hold up well to a fair amount of abuse. It also floats, slightly, compared to the Tooblites that sink like rocks. As such, I think this is the most useful of the UVPaqlite products, for my needs. I have mine in my bedroom, next to a flashlight, attached to a quick-access gun safe. In the event I'm in my room, and the lights instantly go out, I can immediately see where my flashlight is - even before my eyes have adjusted to the dark (though I also have emergency lighting for additional assistance). In a pinch, the UVPaqlite Mini is strong enough that I could find my backup flashlight, or open my safe.

Of the 4 UVPaqlite products I purchased, I'd say that this is my personal favorite. I think the combination of convenient size and brightness make it the most versatile for my needs. I intend to get more of these, and use them to tag several other handy items I'd want to be able to immediately find, in the event of a power outage. As well, they're light enough and small enough, I can easily pin them to my clothing, whenever I go outside at night and wish to remain visible. They also glow like crazy, under a UV black light, which would make them fun at parties.

With these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products, they certainly have their uses - however, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescent glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: UVPaqlite Mini (6 x 4)

text_fidelity_a:
Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer) We have three sets of kitchen knives; a low quality TV infomercial special, a medium quality Chicago Cutlery set, and what we consider high quality home knives by J.A. Henckels. Plus we have more working knives than I care to count. I have used a lot of sharpeners and edge straighteners over the decades but we only use those now for machetes that my wife won't let me use in the Chef's Choice 120. They'd fit too!

I bought the 120 for my wife two years after I bought her the J.A. Henckels knives. New, the knives were amazing; felt like they had a near surgical edge. I knew once they got dull or burred we didn't have anything that would restore them to like-new condition. Before we bought the 120 we took our dull Chicago Cutlery knives to a professional butcher for sharpening to see what we'd get back. We were not impressed with the results so I knew we needed to find a good knife sharpener.

After reading the reviews on sharpeners, I chose the Chef's Choice 120. We carefully read the directions and practiced our technique on the cheap knives. Wow, talk about impressed with the results. Then we put the dull Chicago Cutlery knives through all three stages on the 120. Several of the knives were so dull we had to three-stage them three times to recover the edge. When we were finished they sliced effortlessly through paper! They had NEVER been that sharp, even new. They are decades old knives and I will admit the 1st stage of the 120 did put some scratches on the blades about 1/4" up from the edge, but we didn't care. We just wanted a razor sharp edge on the old knives and the 120 delivered.

We tested stage two and three on some loose knives we had to see if those stages scratched the knife blade. They didn't. Most knives that are maintained properly only require stage two and three, or only stage 3. Once we were confident of no scratches we used only the Stage 3 polishing strop stage on the newer J.A. Henckels. Although the knives were two years old and still exceptionally sharp, they had not been sharpened since we bought them. Plus they had developed a few small burrs. The 120 Stage 3 strop stage removed the burrs, restored the near surgical, like-new edge, and no scratches either. My wife was thrilled with the results!

We use the Stage 3 strop stage on several serrated knives we own and they are noticeably improved and shaper. I've used the 120 on my working pocket knives too. I thought they were acceptably sharp using a diamond edge straightener but the 120 takes sharpening to a completely new level.

The 120 will get hot sharpening a bunch of knives one right after the other, but we typically limit our sharpening to ten knives or less. Stage 1 definitely does scratch the blade but that stage is only recommended for hopelessly dull knives.

Others may have issues with the 120. Not us. Once you understand the technique you need to use with the sharpener, it works great! We love it!
text_fidelity_b: Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Oak Leaf Ultra Bright Portable LED Camping Lantern for Outdoor,Emergency,Hurricanes,Hiking,Hunting,Storm (Black, Collapsible) Given the price, I was expecting a smaller and flimsier lantern, but this turned out to be a fairly robust LED lantern. Powered by only 3 AA batteries, and featuring an array of bluish-white LED emitters set in reflectors, the light output is surprisingly good. It floods the area with very usable light, easily capable of filling a small room or a 10' radius outside in the open. This is about the right amount of light I would want when walking through the woods, changing a tire, or cooking at a campground. You can clearly see what you are doing, can see/read details, but won't be blinded. You can lower the light output by lowering the array into the body, but it doesn't turn off the LEDs so you will still discharge the batteries as quickly.

The overall quality is very good, and I consider it a great light for the price. This product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review, and I'm considering the value based on the regular price. Unlike a few other lanterns in the price range, there is no audible hum when turned on. The light output is comparable to other lights in it's price range, and even a few other higher-priced lanterns, though won't match the high-end lanterns. While the build quality is good, it's also not nearly as rugged as some of the more-expensive lanterns out there. This lantern seems like it would resist a light splash or sprinkle of water, here and there, but would not likely hold up to driving rain or a dunk. Still, for the money, it's a good casual use light for quick backyard usage, and the occasional utility usage.
text_fidelity_b: Oak Leaf Ultra Bright Portable LED Camping Lantern for Outdoor,Emergency,Hurricanes,Hiking,Hunting,Storm (Black, Collapsible)

CamelBak Crux 3-Liter Water Reservoir - Hydration Bladder - Faster Water Flow Rate - Leak-Proof Water Bladder - Ergonomic Shape - Big Bite Valve - BPA-Free - 100oz, Blue I recently took the 3L Crux on a 5 day/4 night backpacking trip in the desert. Some days I had it filled up all of the way, other times just to the 1L mark. I was happy with its performance.

The Crux feels well constructed -- it should be able to withstanding getting banged around in my backpack for many trips to come.

I liked the feel of the bite valve and the divided compartments in the bladder is a smart way to reduce sloshing.

My major complaint is that it's a bit too easy to incorrectly screw the lid on. Looking straight on from the front it can appear to be sealed but it's not and water leaks out. Before you leave the water source where you're filling up you need to tilt the bladder downwards to check that the lid has been properly sealed (if you look at it from the side while twisting the lid you can see if it's going on wrong or right). I suppose this is the price of having the bladder opening on the side — as opposed to the top — which makes it easy to fill holding with one hand, especially in shallow sinks.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Crux 3-Liter Water Reservoir - Hydration Bladder - Faster Water Flow Rate - Leak-Proof Water Bladder - Ergonomic Shape - Big Bite Valve - BPA-Free - 100oz, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Sevylor Big Basin 3-Person Inflatable Kayak with Adjustable Seats & Carry Handles, Heavy-Duty PVC Construction for Rugged Use & Boston Valve for Easy Inflation/Deflation Sevylor calls this a kayak, but kayaks traditionally have covered decks, fore and aft, with a cockpit that you sit in. That was before "sit-upon" kayaks became a thing. This Big Basin is an open boat that you sit or kneel in, which in my mind makes it a canoe, although without the upswept bow and stern of most canoes. Regardless of what you call it, I have found this to be a good size for paddling on reasonably calm water, with two people and a little bit of gear.

I purchased mine primarily for shuttling between my anchored motorboat and shore, for camping, picnicking, beachcombing, or whatever. It works well for that purpose. The inflated boat is light enough for one person to hoist onto the top of my bigger boat's cabin, and to get it down and launched without a winch, a helper, or other drama. I can easily paddle it myself, or we can fit 1 or 2 more people in, as necessary. There isn't a lot of extra room, though. two people and a couple of day packs (and maybe fishing poles) pretty much fills the boat. I don't think that I'd want to try a multi-day camping trip for 2 in it, unless it was clear from the start that this would have to be an ultra-light adventure.

The sides of this boat are fairly low to the water, so it isn't a particularly dry ride. My kayak paddles have drip guards, which helps some, but I usually plan to get wet when paddling this boat. Choppy seas can easily splash in. None of this should come as a surprise to experienced paddlers. I usually wear rain pants or waders when using the boat.

A big advantage is that this boat can be deflated and stowed, or shipped as luggage to a distant destination. I used a similar Sevylor a few years ago on a moose hunt, and found it really useful for paddling back and forth across a lake by camp, and for floating out a quartered moose in one trip (two people walking the boat through the shallows, with a line on each end). I haven't had a chance to use this boat that way yet, but I'm certain that it would work just as well.

I do recommend that you buy a good quality foot pump, and take it with you on whatever paddling adventure takes you away from civilization. The nylon cover fabric is tough, so punctures are likely to be rare, but you can always develop a leak from a loose valve.

Let me know if you find my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Sevylor Big Basin 3-Person Inflatable Kayak with Adjustable Seats & Carry Handles, Heavy-Duty PVC Construction for Rugged Use & Boston Valve for Easy Inflation/Deflation

text_fidelity_a:
Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30

It can do one of two things, it can be a batting tee - which, whilst it does it well, the construct is a tad tacky - the head on the base that holds the ball is openly marked as heat shrink tape, and whilst I have no problem with that being the item used to build it, I expect to not see the ingredients list on a quality item. I also worry about the heat tape being affected if the unit is left in a vehicle on a hot day (a very likely situation).
The soft toss feature is excellent. You set some balls on the top of the unit, switch it on, then every 6 to 10 seconds (depending on the setting) another ball is launched, gently.
I really like this - you can practice alone, easily set it up time and again. The height at which the ball is launched from is easily adjustable to a huge range of heights.
The tripod base is very stable. It is all put together quite superbly. A great device for practicing!

text_fidelity_a:
Personalized Sea turtle Mothers Ring with CZ Platinum Plating Rings for Mother's Day Gift (JQWL) My nickname has been turtle since I was 3 yo, thanks to my dearly departed dad who also happened to be my best friend. My dad was pretty much a single parent who had to be both my father & my mother, until he met my “adoptive mother” when I was 18 yo.
This past Christmas my “mom” got me this ring as a gift but she pointed out that it wasn’t a ring from my “ mother” but it was a gift from my dad who spent many years being a mother to me. My “adoptive mother” got me a different ring altogether from a mother to her daughter & I’ve cherished both of my rings since I put them on. Unfortunately the baby turtle fell off the mama turtle w/in the first 24 hours of receiving it. I’ve done numerous searches to find where the ring came from (my adoptive mother has early stages of Alzheimer’s so she couldn’t remember where she got the ring) I still cherish my ring for what it stands for but I really wish the baby was still intact. I thought if I could find where she bought the ring from I could just buy a replacement ring w/the baby attached so it would it would make me feel better but now that I finally found the same original ring I realized that it has nothing to do w/the ring itself, but more what it signifies to me.
It seems pretty obvious that the ring has a major defect & the baby turtle falls off on most of the reviews so I won’t bother trying to replace it anyway but I would give it WAY more than 5 stars if the baby didn’t fall off.
I’m giving it 3 stars regardless bc of the sentimental value. It’s not fancy & doesn’t look expensive but if you understand the turtle “lifestyle” then I would recommend this ring.
It’s just one of those things, if you know, then you’ll get it. 🐢
Long live the slow & steady lifestyle. You might not win any races but you’ll definitely be able to appreciate everything else along the way 😊
text_fidelity_b: Personalized Sea turtle Mothers Ring with CZ Platinum Plating Rings for Mother's Day Gift (JQWL)

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Unisex The Timex Run Trainer 2.0 is great low profile watch with accurate heart rate monitoring and GPS tracking. It does have several unexpected shortcomings, especially when considering the price and its label as "Ironman".

Nice size. This is one of the smaller heart rate w/ GPS watched I've seen. It fits well, even on my smallish wrists.

Fast connection to GPS - usually took less than 15 seconds, which is pretty good I think.

The memory on this watch is too small, especially considering the price. It seems to hold only about 10 hours of data before it becomes full. Timex should really include a much larger memory chip - aren't they pretty cheap these days?

Biking: Even though there isn't a biking mode, you can switch from pace to speed, which basically makes it a cyclocomputer, in conjunction with the GPS data. You can use the data with online software, including recent support by Strava Cycling.

Swimming: This watch (eventhough it is an Ironman), doesn't technically support swimming. It is waterproof to 50m, which should be good enough for most swimmer. Unfortunately the GPS does not work underwater, even just a foot a water - so you completely lose GPS tracking while swimming. Major bummer. There is a work around I've read about: Place the watch under your swimming cap, so that it usually remains above the water. That seems to help with the GPS, but since the buttons on this watch are very sensitive, you do need to play around with the orientation of the watch so one does not get pressed unintentionally.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Unisex

text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle Computer Wireless Speedometer, Big Number Display Waterproof Automatic Wake-up Stopwatch with LCD Backlight, Speed Distance Time Measure Temperature Consumption Cycling Accessories I bought this to replace a Specialized computer that only lasted a few years, regardless of battery changes.

The Good:
1. It's relatively inexpensive.
2. It's wireless (between the wheel sensor and the computer), which is *amazing* at this price.
3. The display is decent.
4. I prefer two-button over one-button bike computers.
5. If you have a very oddball configuration, it can handle it.

The Bad:
Oh my, let's count the ways.
1. Somewhat unclear manual
2. Incomplete manual - missing super-common bicycle tire sizes. I bought this for a Trek DS8 commuter bike, which has a 700x38. Not listed.
3. Their solution to that? Roll the bike carefully along the ground and measure it. Yeah, right. I guessed, and will work it out later.
4. Unrealistic specs. The manual is clear that the magnet must come within 5mm (1/2cm or less than 1/5th of an inch) of the sensor. Which is not realistic. Compounding this, their magnet's shape requires it be mounted where spoke cross... which many bikes have another mounting point at.
Fortunately, it isn't really that picky.
5. To change the computer mount orientation, you must unscrew four-to-five (seriously, depending on desired orientation) tiny itty bitty screws, re-orient, and replace all or nearly all (seriously... you may no longer have access to some holes) of them.
6. The display is decent, but it really doesn't resemble the one in the photos. In reality, it's much lower contrast (and, of course, not as large as the photos imply, but normal size for a bike computer.)
7. You get, seriously, about 15 seconds after inserting the battery to choose MPH vs KPH... but... much of that time is spent getting the battery door back on and flipping it over. I don't think there's a way to do it other than initially. (To switch it at that point, hit the RIGHT side button. Oddly, the "Mode" button doesn't change modes between K and M, and it doesn't stand for Miles ;)... if you hit M, you have to take out the battery and try again.)

That sounds pretty bad. But all of this is first-time-setup stuff. It really is a VERY nice bike computer even for much more than the price. I'll provide more updates after I've calibrated the tire correctly.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Computer Wireless Speedometer, Big Number Display Waterproof Automatic Wake-up Stopwatch with LCD Backlight, Speed Distance Time Measure Temperature Consumption Cycling Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included) This laser comes with six batteries and you only need three so you have one set for backup. The laser itself in my opinion works good and is bright with a thin beam. You can adjust the beam with the included tool. The attached button cord also works good. I could turn it on and off easily and it always worked properly. Mounting the laser was also a non-issue and tightened good.

The problem with this laser is the button switch located on the back cover of the laser. I had a horrible time getting it to work properly. After studying this thing for awhile, I discovered after removing the battery cover that the spring was crooked and would move the batteries out of position. The result was that the spring tension and spring not making center contact was causing the laser to not work properly. The spring was loose and wobbly too. I tried bending it to center but it only made it worse. My husband had spare various size springs in his shop so was able to remake one that fit better. After about an hour of work we finally got it fixed. I had to make sure the spring was dead center when closing the cap so the batteries wouldn't move out of place and had enough tension so when pressing the on/off button it would work. Another little issue is the batteries do not fit perfect inside the case and are a bit wobbly. So there is that.

I hope you have better luck and maybe this was a glitch in the one I received. I really believe the switch could have been designed better. After all, you want the laser to work when you need it. I cannot in all honesty give this item more than 3 stars and I would not recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included)

text_fidelity_a:
iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black I am surprised at how functional this little gadget is. My smartphone fits right into the protective case and the tiny speakers plug into my phone's headset jack. I can play music or talk on the phone.

* One thing that is especially nice for me is that it holds my phone securely in place and zips shut. I like that because I have one of those phones with a slide-out keyboard - making the rubberized protective case an awkward fit, and the protective case that fits my phone will not stay on. I have dropped my phone several times without any protection and I am surprised that it hasn't broken. This case solves that problem, by containing the entire phone zipped in. It is VERY protective and secure.

* Another thing I like is that the speakers (though small) have a surprisingly good sound. I can listen to music or audio books easily, as long as there is no loud noise around to drown out the sound. This is especially pleasing to me because my phone speakers are not really loud enough to hear much and I have a lot of trouble with my bluetooth device. Since the audio is not wireless and plugs directly into the headset jack, it really simplifies my listening experience.

* Additionally, the speaker jack is not confined to a cell phone. My laptop had terrible sound and when I want to give it a boost, I plug this little device into my computer's headset jack and it gives me just the amount of volume I need without having to mess with bulky speakers.

The negatives are:

* This case is larger than some people would like. I don't mind it, but if you like to carry your cell phone in your pocket, you will not be able to do that while the phone is in this case. It fits nicely into a purse, though.

* The audio uses 2 AA batteries and does not interface with your phone battery. The case cannot be recharged or plugged in, but you will need to continually replace batteries. So far, I have had this case for a week and use it constantly. It still has the original two batteries that I put into it. Your phone will need to be recharged separately from the audio case.

* If you use your phone for other functions besides simply listening to music or talking, they you have to take it out of the case. When secured in this case, the phone is not accessible except for the audio and for answering calls. You will not be able to make calls, use navigation, check email, etc, unless you take your phone out of the case. Again, this isn't a problem for me, but a lot of people like to have their phone immediately accessible for all functions.

* While the sound is perfectly adequate for inside a car or indoors, I think it might be a challenge to hear it well outdoors. This is a SMALL case wirh SMALL speakers - think old fashioned transistor radio. This is NOT a boombox! ;-) If I want to listen to music outdoors, I use headphones. This functions well if I am driving, sewing, or doing dishes, etc.

All in all, I am getting a lot of use from this device. I really love it and don't know how I ever got along without it. I can see how it might not serve everyone's needs but it is great for mine.
text_fidelity_b: iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black

Next time be honest in your commercial and focus on the user experience more than on being cute.

text_fidelity_a:
Pedallon USB Rechargable LED 100 Lumens Front Bike Light I purchased both lamps, the front (white light) and rear (red light). The rear red would a very good rear lamp except the amount of light emitted to each side (of both front and rear lamps) is very close to zero so they are effectively seen only from the front and rear -- not the sides.

The front lamp has no conventional lens with which to focus and amplify the light so it spreads a very wide beam when mounted horizontally or a very tall beam when mounted vertically. Essentially, it casts light to places you don't need to see. The front beam casts only to about four or five feet. I have a very inexpensive single-LED lamp (two AA batteries) that has a focusing lens which casts a directed a beam that is a little brighter and casts a few feet longer.

The lithium-ion batteries charge with a conventional mini-USB cable. A cable is included but no AC adapter is included. They require 2 hours to charge. That it is rechargeable is not much advantage. At the highest intensity the batteries last less than two hours. Most modest LED lamps using convention AA or AAA batteries will last in excess of 40 hours or more. On an overnight trip or a bicycle tour a conventional AA powered lamp would be a far better choice.

The manual states that "the battery may become ineffective at about 80% of its value after 300 to 500 charge/discharge cycles ... 5 years life span under good care." 300 charges sounds closer to 1- to -2 years in my cycling universe. The manual further states that the battery "loses 1% of its charge per day when stored at room temperature and 5% per day at temps over 104F degrees. Stored battery life decreases 50% at freezing and further degrades as temperatures decrease."

The white front lamp is perhaps better used for other purposes, a dark closet or cupboard, for example. I returned the red lamp but will keep the front lamp for a cupboard. Now that I have it for that other use it will still see some limited use on my bicycle but next time I will make another choice for my cycling needs.
text_fidelity_b: Pedallon USB Rechargable LED 100 Lumens Front Bike Light

text_fidelity_a:
TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility I'm very impressed with suspension strap workouts. Doing strength training, instant adjustments to resistance are possible just by adjusting by an inch or two how close you are to the anchor. And almost every strength exercise, whether for arms or legs, also involves the core. Which is amazing.

But the best thing about the straps are for stretching and flexibility. I can get deeper, longer, more supported stretches with these then with any other method I've ever tried. And my friends have called me a stretch fanatic for years.

This DVD gives detailed descriptions of 10 or 12 stretches, with progressions for each one. Their "workout" is about 45 min. long. Or you can use the "exercise library" which gives detailed descriptions of each with their progressions. Watch the exercise library for a much shorter stretch workout or pause with your remote to work an individual stretch longer.

You can probably find most of these stretches on the internet, but I'm glad I got this DVD which I got in a 3 DVD package that included a strength and cardio DVD. The strength is a pretty good workout. Haven't tried the cardio yet.

Notice I haven't mentioned TRX once yet in this review. Although I do own a TRX and like it, you can get VERY similar suspension straps on Amazon for $24.99. I got RopeInaBag and use it for travel because it is much lighter and more compact while still being plenty strong.

Regardless of the brand of straps you use, I highly recommend the stretches in this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility

NordicTrack T Series Treadmills I ordered this machine to try to do something (beside eating) during quarantine.
My husband put it together in a couple of hours. The only time he needed my help was to assemble the parts that goes under the machine that makes it able to fold.
Once ready it is pretty sturdy. Obviously not as the ones at the gym, but mostly because it is smaller. The “bed” is shorter than the pro, but that’s exactly why it is perfect for a house, in my case for my garage. It is somewhat light weight. You can move it a little.
As soon as you press start it ask you to connect it with IFIT. I did not do that. I pressed the iFit button for 30 seconds and it was override. You CAN use it without the app. BUT, I bought the 5’’ screen. I can’t watch anything more than my stats there. Maybe if you buy the machines with larger screens the iFit app could be a good idea. It depends on your likes. But you can totally use this model without the app (6.5s)
The machine is very smooth. No weird sound beside the normal sound of the belt running.
This machine does not have a fan (I don’t need it) , and has good speakers.
I do mostly sprints, so I move from power walking with encline for 1 minute to all out for 1 minute for 15-20 min, and the machine works perfectly in those speeds and incline changes. It does change the speed fast. So you need to be attentive.
My 5’’ screen shows me cal, distance, time, laps...
The folding process is super easy! And like I said before it is not super heavy, and when going down to the floor is smooth, soft and slow. It does not fall fast.
It has a space where you can put your phone or tablet on the front. 2 cup (or towels or whatever) holders on the sides. And the STOP button with the strap for emergency.
Since “we” put it together I’ve been using it everyday. And I really like it. I could definitely recommended it.

Abahub 22PSI SUP Electric Air Pump, Auto-Off Inflation & Deflation, Portable High Pressure Pump, 12 DV Car Connector for Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Boards, Kayaks, Boats After trying a dozen other pumps of various brands I kept coming back to this one. I have tried it on 5 different brands of SUP boards and each time it has been consistent. Filling up each board to 15 psi within 9 to 9.5 minutes. I have pumped up 3 SUPs in a row without any issues. It doesn't heat up the pump or hose nearly as much as others I have tried. Took this pump out on labor day to the beach. But instead of using my vehicle to pump this up I bought the Jackery Portable Power Station Explorer 300 (Which is smaller than a toaster). Walked everything down to the beach and pumped up all SUPs right next to the water. It was great not having to worry about moving boards from your vehicle down to the beach. Just be careful not to get sand or dirt in the connections so they get a tight seal.

One note I would like to mention. When I tried this pump with the 12v in my suv and the engine wasn't running the pump did preform at a slower rate about 11 minutes for 15 psi. I would recommend you have the engine running if you want the pump to perform at the better time around 9 minutes.

For comparison my boards are 10.5 feet and 33 inches wide. I also have an 11.5 foot also.

I also want to caution you, that there are other pumps that look exactly like this pump being sold on Amazon. Externally they may look the same but the motor/pump inside is not the same thing and does not pump them up nearly so quickly, they also heat up a lot more.
text_fidelity_b: Abahub 22PSI SUP Electric Air Pump, Auto-Off Inflation & Deflation, Portable High Pressure Pump, 12 DV Car Connector for Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Boards, Kayaks, Boats

text_fidelity_a: Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks These poles come with a lightweight, durable zippered carrying case and four (8 total) pole end attachments for leaves, snow, blunt-end, and curved trekking. All the attachments alone are accessories that you have to purchase separately with many more expensive pole sets. The snow and leaf attachments are plastic, screwed onto the poles with threads, and the other two are rubber push-on. These are a single-clamp design for length adjustment and compact storage. They have very nice, comfortable wrist straps. With the extensions retracted, their stored length is 31 inches. They have carbide tips at the ends of the poles and the grips are a firm foam material. I love the “lower grip” on each pole, which is great for when you are trekking steep uphills and need to grip the poles in a lower position, or if you are traversing side-hill and need one pole shorter on the uphill side. I can tell you that these poles are extremely light at 5.5 ounces per pole. I have a set of CMT poles that are a two-clamp design at 7.6 ounces each. I can honestly say, in the whole of all of my hiking/backpacking equipment, I know of no other equipment that delivers the quality and light weight compared to price as these poles. When our treadmill started failing after 15 years she cancelled her gym membership and we decided it was time to try something new. Due to hip issues (me) and knee issues (both of us) we needed something that would be comfortable, quiet, give the old heart a boost, and not aggravate our joint issues. The Exerpeutic 300SR exceeded our all our expectations.

My wife actually put the bike together when I was under the weather. The frame is strong and compact. The seat/backrest is comfortable. The mechanism is whisper quiet, quieter than any exercise bike we've ever used. Why lay on the couch watching TV when you can comfortably sit on the bike and do the same thing? The only weak part is the display. Hands off! It works absolutely fine but I can already see it breaking if someone tries to put their weight on it while getting on or off the bike. We've put a label on it that says "Not a handle - will break" to prevent occasional guests from making that mistake.

If the Exerpeutic 300SR lasts only three months, we're still ahead of what the gym membership cost. I suspect it will last much longer.

Update: 6 months and this baby gets a workout twice a day on most days, me in the morning and my wife in the evening. Still working perfectly!

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny SF-B1110 Indoor Cycling Bike I used to be a very active and fit person. I spent 12 years in the Army and as recently as 10 years ago was still running 3 miles a day. However the past 10 years have not been kind; I've gotten older (51), I work at a desk all day and have gotten fat (50lbs+ overweight) and have started having problems with my feet and knees. I knew I needed to get back in shape, but running was out due to my feet and knees. Seeing the Peloton advertisements on TV got me interested in spinning as it seemed like an intense workout that wouldn't kill my feet and knees. Looking into Peloton and seeing the insane price for the bike and classes, and the fact that to use their classes you need an iPhone, iPad, or Apple TV I started looking around for something more affordable that would work with something besides Apple.

That research led me to the Sunny SF-B1110. Based on other reviews the bike had everything that I was looking for; heavy flywheel, sturdy construction, handlebars adjustable front and back and up and down, not noisy and the price was right ($279.99).

I ordered the bike and it arrived in three days. The box it arrived in had slight damage to the outside which is not unexpected with the weight of the item, but the bike itself was packed and cushioned quite well and had no damage. The bike comes 90% assembled, so the only things you need to put together are the front and rear stabilizer bars (the bars that sit on the floor, four bolts total), mount the handlebars and post, mount the seat and post, attach the pedals and you're done.

PROS:
- Price
- Solid Construction
- Fit and Finish
- Quiet Chain Drive
- Smooth Resistance Adjustment
- Front and Back Handlebar Adjustment
- Flywheel Weight

CONS:
- Seat
- Only Three Up/Down Handlebar adjustment holes

Once assembled the bike itself really good looking. The paint is thick and clean, chrome is well done, flywheel is well balanced and spins with no wobble. Chain is quiet and smooth and the resistance adjustment knob works smoothly (doubles as the emergency brake).

The seat that the bike comes with is one of the cons. It's hard, cheaply made and painful to use, especially if you are overweight. Some people will claim you just need to get used to the narrow seats that seem to be the norm now, but the kind of pain this seat caused you can't get used to. I purchased this seat for the bike, [[ASIN:B000H87PUI Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black]] and it made all the difference in the world. I highly recommend it and it attaches to the seat post with no modification.

The other con is the vertical adjustment of the handlebars. The handlebar post has only three adjustment holes (the seat post has five). I'm a little over 6 feet tall and have the seat adjusted to its highest point point which puts the seat higher than the handle bars at their highest adjustment point. This very uncomfortable, especially if you have a big belly like I do. I solved this issue by drilling two additional adjustment holes in the handlebar post. There was plenty of room for the additional holes, so why the manufacturer didn't do this is not clear. The handle bars now sit slightly higher than the seat and is much more comfortable.

I also purchased several other items to go with the bike. For anybody that's out of shape you really need to use a heart monitor to make sure you aren't harming yourself by overdoing your workout. I ordered the [[ASIN:B00INQVYZ8 Wahoo TICKR Heart Rate Monitor for iPhone & Android]] and it works very well with my android phone. I also ordered the [[ASIN:B00L9XNFPY Wahoo RPM Cadence Sensor for iPhone, Android and Bike Computers]] to help me sync my workout with the class I'm taking. I also added these clipless pedals [[ASIN:B0014UG3WE Shimano PD-A530 Sport Dual-sided Pedal]].

As far as the classes, I found SweatStudio online classes. Unlike Peloton, they work with Android, PC, Roku, Chromecast, etc. and they have more than spin (yoga, TRX, etc.). I cast my classes onto my 51 inch TV which is much better than some 9 inch tablet.

So for about $500 and some customizing I've got a full workout setup. So far I've lost a few pounds, but more importantly my heart and lungs are getting noticeably stronger. I can't recommend this bike more highly.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny SF-B1110 Indoor Cycling Bike

text_fidelity_a:
EastPoint Sports Foosball Table Soccer Game with Steal Player Rods, Bead Style Scoring, and 4 Foosball Balls This is a nice home table. I can see it even being used in an AirBNB style vacation rental. It lacks balanced players and likely cannot handle years of abuse, but it also has a modest price and gets shipped right to your door in a couple days!

With casual (though loads of fun) home use in mind, it's great! It took some time and effort to assemble, but once built, it's built to last. As noted, it's not a commercial grade unit, but even vigorous home use won't do this any harm. The players spin and move freely, and the ball isn't overly keen to fly who knows where.

In the end this is a MDF table, not a hardwood or metal one. It's heavy, and it won't last forever (I think multiple moves would be the death of it--that or moisture if used where that's an issue). I think 5-10 years of use in a home rec room is a reasonable expectation however. For the price, it's worth it.

text_fidelity_a:
Masters Macrolight Adjustable Length Bi-Material Carbon Aluminum Trekking Poles (Black, 60-135-cm) I loved how light they are. These are really well made poles, but I returned them unused. With no gloves on, I couldn't set the length, lock in place and lean on them to simulate a fall without them slipping. And no way could I lock them with gloves on. This is not a knock on the manufacturer. Twist lock mechanisms are bound to fail over time. These would probably be excellent in the summer when you are not wearing gloves. The foam handles are firm get giving. Not sure how absorbent the handles are.

The final thing I learned, which I'll try to confirm with other carbon poles, is that there is significant vibration when you smack a pole down (I was simulating on carpet). Man, these poles resonate! You feel it in your hands. This might not be a bad thing. For carbon fiber bicycles, the give in the material creates a dampening effect. This could be a great alternative to an active shock absorbing mechanism. We'll see...

UPDATE 02/12/2014
I bought Leki carbon poles and went did 4k+ vertical, 2k+ in snow. Yes, you want carbon. The lighter the better! I'm new to snowshoeing, so I fell a few times. They took the bend. The give in the poles is the right amount of dampening for me. Perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Masters Macrolight Adjustable Length Bi-Material Carbon Aluminum Trekking Poles (Black, 60-135-cm)

text_fidelity_a:
Neso Tents Beach Tent with Sand Anchor, Portable Canopy Sunshade - 7' x 7' - Patented Reinforced Corners Ack, my husband and I just took our new Neso Tent down to the beach today ... and lasted about 45 minutes under scanty shade with not enough head room. We SO wanted to love this shelter, as it has a brilliant concept: idiot-proof setup and very transportable kit, with the fabric and two collapsible poles all in one tidy storage bag.

In looking at the videos and even pictures of this particular model of Neso Tent, it appears that WIND is a HUGE factor in one's satisfaction with the overall experience. Alas, we sat on a hot, sunny, windless beach by the lake, so we found the fatal flaw real fast: without wind to literally LIFT the fabric up in the air, it sits flat and low at back. We could barely fit our slim selves in two beach chairs under that fabric. With the poles lifting up the front, the back of the fabric slopes down so low that our heads literally poked into the fabric overhead like two beach balls. Duh.

Not only that, but even on a windless beach, you're gonna need some serious LEAD weight to hold the 4 corner ropes in place. We hunted around our beach and found 3- to 5-lb river rocks. Once you raise the poles under the fabric, it literally lifts the corner ropes up in the air unless they are weighted down GOOD. To show a few handfuls of sand tossed into each pouch doing the job is simply misleading, unless that sand is made from lead shot.

On top of which, in order to face the view - i.e., the lake - we had the sun slanting in from the side. As soon as we set the tent up, that meant that one of us sat with legs in the burning SUN the whole time. Yes, even with our chairs scooched back so far that our dorky heads poked into the fabric, the total shaded area of this fabric is simply too small, measuring about 6' square. We probably could've re-positioned the tent with our backs facing the sun, but then we would've been staring at two bikini-clad gals lying on their beach towel 5 feet away - kind of in-your-face? Nope. It was no go.

Frustrated, we packed the tent up and will be sending it back. I think the perfect beach shelter should actually be more like a camping tent, with full coverage overhead and multiple, collapsible poles strung through the structure. Ideally, this tent would have net sides to let the breeze come through (and probably filtered sun). Most of the tents I see here are simply too HOT and airless, cuz they're made more for all-weather camping. Or they're shelters like 8' tall and 12' wide, which - if the two of us parked that on our little lakeside beach - would encourage others to beat us with their rubbah slippahs.

Best way to enjoy the beach is to slather up in sunscreen, leave all the food, drink, books and stuff at home. Go with a towel and get in the water. Period.
text_fidelity_b: Neso Tents Beach Tent with Sand Anchor, Portable Canopy Sunshade - 7' x 7' - Patented Reinforced Corners

text_fidelity_a:
UST Emergency Food Ration Bars (PDQ 4-ct) Bought locally to try before placing a large order.

Taste is pretty neutral, kind of like a fig newton without the fig. Not bad at all, and not good enough that anyone is going to crave them or get into them short of a real need. This is not a gourmet meal or an enticing snack, it is not meant to provide complete nutrition, it is meant to get a person through a rough situation, and allowances have been made for that.

With the above in mind, this product earned two stars because these are so hard and so compressed that anyone without solid teeth is going to have a really difficult time eating them. They do NOT soften in liquid due to the oil content(most compact way to add calories), and the individual bars themselves are too large to be eaten without being broken apart, which may also be difficult depending on what tools and abilities a person has.

Really recommend the Datrex brand survival rations instead. All the pluses, plus easy to eat. When the chips are down and you're busting into your survival rations, there's really no reason to make it any more difficult than it already is.

text_fidelity_a: Crosman Zombie Resettable Steel Field Target This resettable target is just plain fun to shoot.  It works perfectly. Even after 50 shots the target was still resetting perfectly and did not move even in the wet muddy ground.  Yes the face gets beat up pretty bad (as far as the paint job goes). but I didn't buy it for the looks lol.  I only use a .177 call putting out about 15 to 18 ft/lbs of energy so no dents or dings on the metal plates.  I would be comfortable shooting this with a .22 airguns also but anything with more energy would most likely leave dents.  Also only use softer pellets (lead) as harder alloys or BBs will bounce back.  With proper care and a little paint this target should last for 100's of thousands of hits.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. While you can use this as a foot vibrator, I thought to help my wife heal - when cleared by the doctor - she might be able to use that foot massager to advance her healing - but again, I grabbed that because of this company - I was that impressed.

Overall the LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine is a great workout tool and we are happy to have it. I feel like it has added to my workout and will aide me in getting into the shape I’m working towards and my goals.
text_fidelity_b: Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs

Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle My experience with Kryptonite goes back to the period when one of their their original locks was found to be easily opened with a ballpoint pen. I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

One final note - Although I am sure no one else at Amazon would make this foolish mistake, when we left our B&B to head home from our last vacation I locked up the bikes and then left my cord with the keys to both locks draped over one of the handle bars while I checked the pressure on our car tires for the trip home. Of course I forgot about the keys and did not notice they were missing until we got home and tried to take our bikes off the rack. Luckily I was able to go into our house and get the spare keys that came with the locks. When I ordered replacements from Kryptonite they sent me new keys for both locks at no charge. Kryptonite provides excellent locks and they also provide excellent customer service!
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle

text_fidelity_a: Coleman 8-Person Tent | Instant Family Tent This tent is exactly what the reviews said.  It's big and heavy.  That is good and bad.  Bad for those cold summer nights but good because you can stand up in the thing!  Our first experience wasn't the best but I'm hopeful we learned some lessons.  We got up to our campsite without opening and trying everything out first.  BIG MISTAKE.  We couldn't find any stakes, nor does this come with a rain tarp.  (I thought all tents come with those because why wouldn't you need one???)  The forecast was for rain and I was hoping that my 3 young kids and I didn't get rained on.  Luckily, our friends lent us some of their stakes (it was extremely windy) and we made a makeshift a rain tarp out of some other stuff we had.  When we collapsed the tent, it was quite time consuming and the stakes were found UNDER everything.  So watch out for that.  If you go to set up the tent, look underneath it for your stakes.  The extra rain tarp is $50 more and we just bought it off Amazon.  I liked the large windows but there are no ties to hold the unzipped winder covers.  Kind of dumb but I can deal with it.  We are a family of 5 and fit with plenty of room for our stuff.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman 8-Person Tent | Instant Family Tent

The problem with this reflective vest is that the triangular shape you see in the picture here on the product page--there's also one on the back--isn't actually a different shade of yellow, it's a surprisingly dark grey, a second mesh over the yellow you can see for the rest of the vest. This isn't a reflective grey material, it's simply grey, reducing the overall visibility of the rather short vest. I cannot understand why the grey is there; the yellow material is pretty visible, but putting the quite large grey triangle on the front and back makes it much less effective.

I'm disappointed enough that I'll be looking for a replacement.

Suyzufly Men Women Foldable Sling Bags Shoulder Chest Backpack Crossbody Daypack for Cycling Walking Hiking Black I wanted to like this. I really did. It seems small and portable, and yet able to turn into a useful shoulder bag for carryings some stuff.

Except... Take a look at these photos.

First off, it isn't well assembled. The first time I touched the loop that you should be able to connect to a caribiner for ease of carrying when it's folded, it came apart. No pressure here; they just didn't sew it correctly. And when folded up, it's too large to pocket. So that loop would have come in handy.

And it doesn't hold much. The loaded photo shows the bag stuffed, packed to the gills... with only two items - a denim shirt and a small loaf of turkey ham. Nothing else. You could not fit a bath towel, much less a beach towel, in here.

It's a great idea, but find a larger bag, and preferably one that is sewn correctly.

------------------------------------------

Update: We tried to repair it; sewed the flopping end to the other end of the loop. And the first end came out too. As did an unrelated seam. We've thrown this out.

Exped Air Pillow, Medium I bought three of these bad boys mostly based on a whim to have a pillow and the thoughts of comfort when sleeping. I've recently equipped my family to be able to do some decent backpacking. These were sort of afterthoughts.

I based my choices largely on Amazon user reviews. With few exceptions, and I hope we shan't be one, I was taken with the price, size and comfort.

I'm looking forward to giving this a night's use.

EDIT 08-25-2013

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes I ordered two Sunlite (Kenda) Thorn resistant tubes (700c x 18/23) with removable presta core in July of 2015. I wanted a thick (puncture resistant) tube that allowed me to remove the core (with a chain tool) to allow me to inject tire sealant into the tube.

In the Southwest, we have nasty thorns called 'goatheads' that cause many flats. As part of my defense system, I use: 1) a thick, thorn resistant tube, 2) tire sealant (Flat Attack); 3) a high-quality, super puncture-resistant tire (Schwalbe - Marathon Plus Tour, Marathon Supreme, or Durano Plus - depending on the bike).

I waited a while to see how these Sunlite tubes would hold up. Unfortunately, after about a year and a half, the front tube failed. The presta valve stem separated from the tube, rendering the tube unrepairable and useless. The rear tube got a flat, but due to the tire sealant, I was able to simply pump up the tire, spin the wheel, and it sealed itself.

I had high hopes for these tubes, but I will look for other alternatives.

TIP: One reason that many of these tubes may be failing at the stem is due to the threaded, round 'nut' on the valve stem. The nut is really helpful when inflating the tube for the FIRST time, (i.e., when there is no air in it). However, once inflated to full pressure, I would recommend REMOVING this nut and setting it aside. The problem is that when riding with this nut tightened down on the valve stem, it creates added pressure on the stem at the base of the tube, increasing the likelihood of separation & failure.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes
